attempts.entry_title: Optogenetic inhibition in human hippocampal slices on HD-MEAs (Andrews, Geng, Voitiuk et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data: that light on the opsin HcKCR1 suppresses unit firing in human hippocampal slices across culture media and in closed loop, that kainic acid bursts show theta coherence and spread across the granule cell layer, and that waveform clusters over that layer are linked to an opto-response cluster. The dandiset holds raw voltage only, without the curated units these analyses rest on, the light times or labels for each recording's medium. Of the minor claims, the paper's network model, rerun from its code, reproduced the dampening of seizure-like events, and the cohort matches Table 1 except that no file records each slice's opsin.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Andrews, Geng, Voitiuk et al. (2024) on dandiset 001132, which holds 69 raw HD-MEA voltage recordings of 12 human hippocampal slices from 7 patients. The files hold no sorted units, light events or condition labels, so only the cohort claim is tested; the notebook surveys every recording, recovers light periods of slices 3C, 4C and 7D from the voltage, shows a threshold-crossing variant for those of 3C, and runs the paper's network model.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Andrews, Geng, Voitiuk et al. (2024) from dandiset 001132

outcomes.statement: Recordings came from 12 hippocampal slices from 7 adult patients with refractory temporal lobe epilepsy (5 female, 2 male, aged 20 to 52), 8 slices transduced with HcKCR1, 2 with ChR2 and 2 with no opsin.
outcomes.source: Table 1
outcomes.quote: The sex, number and age of participants is detailed in Table 1
outcomes.notes: The 69 files resolve, by their names, to 12 slices named as in Table 1 (1A to 12G) from 7 patients (A to G), 5 female and 2 male, aged 20 to 52, each patient's age and sex as in Table 1. The 8 HcKCR1 slices of Table 2 are present by name. The opsin of a slice is recorded neither in the files nor in the dandiset metadata, so the third expected value (8 HcKCR1 slices) cannot be measured from the dandiset; it follows only from reading the slice names against the paper's Table 1. Every object under general/ of every file was read; it holds the devices, the electrode table, experiment_description (the paper's title), institution, lab, source_script and the subject's age, sex, species and subject_id, with no virus, pharmacology, protocol, notes, optogenetics or genotype field and no opsin or virus word. Of the criterion's conditions, slices, patients, ages and sexes hold (checked against Table 1 in the notebook) and the opsins cannot be resolved, which is read here as partial.
deviations: Assumed reading of the criterion's partial clause. "Present and identifiable" is read as present and identifiable by name, the slice names of the files matching those of Table 1 and Table 2, as no file or metadata field names a slice's opsin. Under a reading that requires each HcKCR1 slice to be identified as HcKCR1 from the dandiset itself, neither clause of the criterion holds.
Slices and patients are taken from the file and subject names (`3C-7` is recording 7 of slice 3C of patient C); `subject_id` itself names the recording, not the patient or slice.

outcomes.statement: In a network model of dentate granule and basket cells, closed-loop activation of a kalium channel in less than 50% of granule cells dampens seizure-like events (10%, 25% and 50% expression shown).
outcomes.source: Results, Computational modeling of glutamatergic neuron inhibition; Extended Data Fig. 3; Methods, Simulation Prototype
outcomes.quote: In silico epileptiform activity could be dampened with optogenetic control of less than 50% of the granule cell population ( Extended data Fig. 3 )
outcomes.notes: The model needs NEST 3.4 with a neuron compiled by NESTML 5 (Simulation/environment.yml at commit 6865bf6, printed in the notebook). PyPI has no NEST 3.4 (its releases are 3.9.0.post0.dev14 and 3.10.0), and with NEST 3.10.0 and NESTML 5.3.0, the newest 5.x, the script's first step, generate_nest_target on the published model, fails (module 'nest.ll_api' has no attribute 'sli_func'). The outcome verified in round 2 was blocked (not_runnable) on that basis. In the final revision, as the round-2 verifier asked, NEST 3.4 is taken from conda-forge in a throwaway environment made with micromamba 2.10.0, with NESTML 5.3.0 and the other packages of the environment file. The model then fails to build twice, first because odetoolbox, unpinned in the environment file, resolves to a release NESTML 5.3.0 cannot call (analysis() got an unexpected keyword argument 'simplify_expression'), and with odetoolbox 2.5 at cmake, because the conda-forge nest-config prints an empty compiler. With nest-config made to print the environment's compiler the model builds, and Simulation/simulation.py runs unchanged, printing mean rates of 80.65, 60.06, 52.49 and 49.65 Hz at opsin fractions 0, 0.10, 0.25 and 0.50 (closed-loop light 0, 16, 11 and 9 times). Events are runs of 1 ms bins with more than 100 spikes over the 1012 cells, the script's opto_threshold. At the script's seed, 20, (a) the total event duration is 278, 124, 37 and 4 ms, (b) the number of events 10, 10, 10 and 4, and (c) the spikes in events 52,366, 17,594, 4,086 and 441. Readings (a) and (c) meet the criterion and (b) does not. With seeds 21, 23 and 24 (a check, the script has one seed), (a) and (c) are at most 0.70 of their value at 0 at every fraction. Seed 22 does not meet the criterion under any reading; the network spends 1 ms above threshold at fraction 0, and at 0.50 the event duration is the same and the spikes in events are 103 against 101 at 0. The verdict uses the script's seed. Reproduced was proposed in the final revision and the round-3 verifier agreed.
deviations: The model is run in an environment built from conda-forge with micromamba, outside the entry's locked pip environment, in a throwaway directory. Besides the environment file's packages it holds cmake 3, a C++ compiler and make from conda-forge, which NESTML 5 needs to build the module, and braingeneers is pinned to 0.3.1.16 (unpinned in the environment file).

odetoolbox, which the environment file leaves unpinned, is set to 2.5 (October 2022, the release current when NESTML 5.2.0, the version the README cites, came out); the newest release fails with NESTML 5.3.0 in the notebook.

The conda-forge nest-config of NEST 3.4 prints an empty --compiler, which leaves the generated CMakeLists without a C++ compiler; it is changed to print the environment's compiler. The model and the script are not changed.
The script is run once as published (seed 20), and its sim() again with seeds 21 to 24, a check the paper does not make.

outcomes.statement: In physiologic media (slice 3C), 10 s of continuous 530 nm light reduces the spontaneous firing of HcKCR1 slices; the rate after light-OFF is higher than during light-ON (ST2).
outcomes.source: Fig. 3a; Extended Data Fig. 4a,b; Supplemental Table ST2 (3C)
outcomes.quote: Constant illumination for 10 seconds reduces spontaneous firing rates ( Fig. 3a )
outcomes.notes: Needs the curated units of 3C, which are not in the dandiset. The light events, also not stored (no GPIO bit or stimulation log), can be recovered for 3C from a step the LED leaves in the voltage of every channel; 3C-6 has 5 trials whose three windows lie in the file and 3C-7 has 6. The onsets of 3C-6 are 18 to 21 s apart, so some of its pre and OFF windows hold part of a neighbouring light period (printed in the notebook). A variant on multi-unit threshold crossings of 64 channels (decides nothing) finds crossings 86 to 90% lower during light in the single-trial files 3C-1 to 3C-5, and no change in 3C-6 (-16%, adjusted p 0.82) or 3C-7 (+6%, p 0.87). Light onset drives 81 to 94% of channels to the ends of the ADC range in the first 0.5 s. In 3C-7, seconds with over 1,000 crossings are 22 of the 54 seconds wholly inside light, 6 of the 12 that hold an onset or offset and 8 of the other 124. With the first second of each window left out, 26 to 52% of channels are still at the ends of the range in the next 0.5 s, crossings fall by 89 to 93% in 3C-1 to 3C-5 and by 18% in 3C-6 (adjusted p 0.77), and rise by 17% in 3C-7 (adjusted p 0.06). The crossings are confounded by saturation and transients either way.

findings.statement: The 69 files hold raw HD-MEA voltage only. The sorted and curated units on which almost every result of the paper rests are not in the dandiset, nor public elsewhere, and the histology and patch-clamp data are not deposited. 27 of the 28 claims on the paper's recordings cannot be tested.

The light ON and OFF times, which the Methods say were stored in the MaxWell file's GPIO bit and in a stimulation log, are not in the files, nor are the light intensities. They can be recovered from a step the LED leaves in the voltage in the eight 3C recordings (on every channel) and in 4C-1, 4C-3, 7D-0, 7D-2, 7D-5 and 7D-7 (on part of the array, steps of 40 to 88 counts). No channel group of any 5C, 8D, 10F or 11G recording shows a 10 s light step, including 10F, which the paper illuminated for 10 trials, and 9E and 12G show none in the first channel group.

No file says which medium, drug or light protocol it was recorded under (physiologic, bicuculline, 0-mg, 0-mg plus kainic acid, closed loop, intensity sweep), which opsin its slice carries, or which of the paper's recordings it is. The session descriptions are empty and the files keep no original recording names, so the paper's per-condition analyses cannot be assigned to files.

Each file's subject_id is the recording (for example 3C-7), so the archive counts 69 subjects where the paper has 7 patients and 12 slices. Every session_start_time is 2024-09-28, the date of the NWB conversion, not of the recording.

The NWB fields for the experiment are empty or absent in every file. general/ holds no virus, pharmacology, protocol, notes, optogenetics, slices or surgery field and no subject genotype, strain or description; experiment_description is the paper's title in all 69 files, and the ElectricalSeries' description and comments are the converter's defaults.

In the 3C recordings, light onset drives 81 to 94% of the channels in the first 64-channel group to the ends of the 0 to 1023 range in the first 0.5 s, and some stay there through the light period. In at least one 5C recording, 34% of that channel group sits at the ends of the range in the median 100 ms bin.
Electrode location is "unknown" for every channel, and nothing places the array over the slice's anatomy (granule cell layer, hilus), which the paper's GCL and propagation analyses use.
The conversion to volts is 6.29 uV per count for slices 1A to 8D and 1.57 uV per count for 9E to 12G, a gain difference that the dandiset does not describe.

attempts.entry_title: Bursting dynamics and circuits in human hippocampal slices (Elliott, Andrews et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: The paper's microcircuit findings hold up with its curated spike sortings: the significant unit pairs (all eight counts exact), the bipolar circuits of the two kainic acid slices and the geometry test reproduce. Its findings on seizure dynamics did not: kainic acid bursting, theta propagation in stages and sub-bursts tracking theta all failed here, largely because neither the paper nor its code defines bursts, onset or stages. Phase-locked units form two spatial clusters only with the code's spike selection, not the Methods', and the STTC clusters hold in one slice of two. The dataset holds raw voltage only, without the sortings, the kainic acid timing or two of the recordings.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Elliott, Andrews et al. (2026) on dandiset 001132, the raw HD-MEA recordings of human hippocampal slices from patients with epilepsy, with the curated spike sortings from the paper's repository. It links the sortings to the raw files, then tests the unit counts, bursting after kainic acid, STTC clustering, circuit pairs, angle histograms and the geometry test from spikes, and theta phase locking, electrode lag clustering, propagation stages and the onset spectrum from the raw voltage.

notebooks.title: Spike-based claims and the link of sortings to raw files
Claims on the raw voltage (phase locking, theta lags, onset spectrum)

outcomes.statement: The curated spike sortings of the paper's repository can be linked to the dandiset's raw recordings; each recording's units sit on the electrodes of one dandiset file, and its spike times align with that file's raw voltage.
outcomes.source: Data Availability; github.com/braingeneers/human_hippocampus at commit 0f83f70, data/ephys and the latency notebooks under figures/figure_3/latencies/t_test_try30_try3
outcomes.notes: Every unit position of each sorting is an electrode position of one slice's files. The offset scan links recordings 1 to 6 to single files with peaks 74 to 169 times the chance level (S1 KA sub-10F-6 from 0 s, S1 baseline sub-10F-0 from 20.0 s, S2 KA sub-11G-2, S2 baseline sub-11G-4, S3 sub-1A-0, S4 sub-9E-2 from 30.0 s). Recordings 7 (S5) and 8 (S6) match the layout of the sub-3C and sub-8D files but no file by time (best ratio 1.3 and 1.4), so their raw recordings are not in the dandiset. The same scan run in lfp_elliott_2026.ipynb gives the same links. Each sorting file is the one the paper's latency notebook for that recording loads (printed with its cell and line). The scan finds the S3 sorting in a 40 s piece of its file (ratio 39 at the expected offset), and every sub-3C file is at least 40 s long, so no sub-3C file holds a stretch of the S5 recording, alone or joined to the others. The unit counts and durations of the linked records are compared in table1-unit-counts.
deviations: A link claim added by the author, as the claims that use the sortings with the raw voltage need the match (protocol, author step 1.4).

outcomes.statement: The eight recordings analysed hold 212, 249, 180, 51, 87, 109, 136 and 100 sorted units (recordings 1 to 8) and last 6, 5, 8.5, 5, 7, 2.2, 6.4 and 1.8 minutes.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Table 1
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Extended Data Table 1, an image in the supplement PDF; no sentence states them.
outcomes.notes: Unit counts are 212, 249, 180, 51, 87, 109, 136 and 100, all equal to the paper's. Durations of the linked dandiset files are 6.00, 5.22, 8.50, 5.01, 6.97 and 2.67 min for recordings 1 to 6; recordings 7 and 8 are not in the dandiset. Five recordings match on both units and duration (S4's file is 2.67 min against 2.2), where the criterion asks for six. The spans of the sortings (6.00, 4.55, 8.50, 5.01, 6.97, 2.17, 6.42, 1.78 min) match all eight durations; the S4 sorting covers 30 to 160 s of its file. The failure is a property of the dandiset (two recordings missing, one held inside a longer file), not a disagreement with the paper's numbers.

outcomes.statement: After kainic acid, slice S1 shows synchronized rhythmic bursting, with about 6 to 8 bursts grouped within larger burst epochs (superbursts).
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 1; Figure 1g and 1h
outcomes.quote: After administering kainic acid to slice S1, synchronized rhythmic bursting activity was observed ... approximately 6–8 bursts grouped within larger burst epochs
outcomes.notes: Under the four readings (threshold a or b, sigma 10 or 20 ms) the median number of bursts per epoch in the first 150 s is 40, 21.5, 22 and 15, and the first epoch holds 4, 2, 3 and 2 bursts; none is in 5.4 to 8.8. The first epoch starts at 0.73 to 0.90 s, before the paper's initiation at 14.4 s; under reading b with sigma 20 the second epoch, which starts at 15.0 s near the paper's initiation, holds 7 bursts, but that is not a reading the criterion names. The median fraction of units whose rate rises at a burst is 0.49 to 0.53, so the synchrony part is borderline. All readings give 12 epochs. Measured is the first reading the criterion lists (reading a, sigma 10, median over the first 150 s). Outside the criterion, merging peaks closer than 500 ms (the code's S1 sub-bursts are 170 to 180 ms apart) gives a median of 7.5 to 10 bursts per epoch (7.5 and 8.0 under reading b) and 60 to 83 bursts in S1; whether the criterion's 50 ms merge counts sub-bursts as bursts is asked of a reader (questions/elliott-2026.yaml).
deviations: Reading a needs the pre-KA part of the KA recording; no time of KA application is recorded and bursting starts within the first second, so the separate baseline recording of the same slice (recorded before KA; Results, paragraph 10) is used as the pre-KA reference, and the recording's own mean for slices without one.
Peaks closer than 50 ms are merged by keeping the higher (scipy find_peaks distance); the synchrony window of +-50 ms around a burst is a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Slice S1 had 67 bursts grouped into 11 superbursts over about 350 s; S2 had 47 bursts, highly synchronized for the first 50 s and sporadic for the next 300 s; in both slices bursts occurred for about 350 s.
outcomes.source: Methods, Classification of Epileptiform-like Events, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 13
outcomes.quote: Slice S1 contained 67 bursts during its seizure-like event. The bursts were highly synchronized and grouped into 11 sets of super bursts over 350 seconds. Slice S2 contained 47 bursts. The bursts for S2 were highly synchronized for the first 50 seconds, but then were sporadic for the next 300 seconds. For both slices, bursts occurred for roughly 350 seconds
outcomes.notes: Under every reading S1 has 12 epochs (within tolerance of 11) over 344 s (within tolerance of 350) but 124 to 353 bursts against 67; S2 has 89 to 157 bursts against 47, a first epoch of 19.4 s against 50 s, and bursts over 486 to 491 s against 350. No reading matches all S1 or all S2 values. In the first 254 s every reading has 9 epochs where the code lists 8 seizure windows, and 90 to 92% of S1 bursts fall in those windows. Measured is reading a, sigma 10.
deviations: The S2 duration of synchronized bursting is read as the span of its first epoch; the paper does not define it.

outcomes.statement: Neural activity increased after kainic acid; the population firing rate rose by 0.5 spikes per second per unit in S1 and 0.9 in S2.
outcomes.source: Methods, Classification of Epileptiform-like Events, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The population firing rate increased by 0.5 spikes per second per unit for S1 and 0.9 spikes per second per unit for slice S2.
outcomes.notes: The mean rate per unit falls from the baseline to the KA recording, S1 4.32 to 4.20 spikes/s (-0.12) and S2 2.38 to 2.28 (-0.10) (reading b); over the bursting period (reading c) the change is -0.03 to -0.05 under every burst reading. Reading a cannot be run, as no time of KA application is recorded. The KA and baseline sortings were curated separately (212 and 249 units in S1, 180 and 51 in S2), so the rates are of different unit sets. The statement's "neural activity increased" does not hold on these sortings.
deviations: Reading a of the criterion is not available for lack of the KA application time.

outcomes.statement: Epileptiform-like activity began in S1 and S2 shortly after kainic acid was applied, within 15 s by one passage of the Methods and within 30 s by another.
outcomes.source: Methods, Tissue preparation, paragraph 1; Methods, Classification of Epileptiform-like Events, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Slices S1 and S2 from the dentate gyrus exhibited epileptiform-like activity within fifteen seconds after the administration of kainic acid.
outcomes.notes: The criterion needs the time of KA application from the dandiset. The files hold no epochs, intervals, annotations or stimulus series, their session descriptions are empty, and the session start times are all the conversion date. The first detected burst is at 0.73 to 0.90 s (S1) and 0.37 s (S2) of the recordings, which bounds the latency only if KA was applied at the recording start, which nothing states.

outcomes.statement: Slice S4 received kainic acid but showed no epileptiform-like behaviour, and none of S3 to S6 showed seizure-like activity.
outcomes.source: Results, last paragraph before Discussion; Extended Data Table 1
outcomes.quote: Notably, slice S4 was administered kainic acid, but did not exhibit any epileptiform-like behavior or the circuit dynamics of S1 and S2.
outcomes.notes: With a burst counted as synchronized when more than half of the units rise (the fig1g criterion's definition of a synchronous burst), S3 to S6 have no synchronized burst under any reading, while S1 has 77 to 138 and S2 89 to 134. S2 has two epochs longer than 10 s (19 s) under every reading; S1 has none, its longest epoch lasting 8 to 10 s. The test finds no sustained synchronized bursting in S3 to S6, the absence the claim states, and the positive control holds for S2 but not for S1, so neither the criterion's reproduced clause (which needs S1 too) nor its not-reproduced clause (any of S3 to S6) applies; partially reproduced. At a fraction of 0.4, S4 to S6 have 1 to 6 synchronized bursts and no epoch longer than 2 s; at 0.6 none. With every burst kept (the first version, which dropped "synchronized"), at least three of S3 to S6 have epochs longer than 10 s (longest 16 to 418 s), as their bursts raise the rate of few units (median fraction 0.15 to 0.34 against 0.49 to 0.74 in S1 and S2). The LFP part of the paper's classification is not tested (claims file).
deviations: Sustained synchronized bursting is read as an epoch (bursts with gaps under 5 s) lasting more than 10 s from its first to its last burst, an assumption; the outcome for S1 rests on it.

A synchronized burst is one in which more than half of the units fire above their mean rate within 50 ms of the peak, from the fig1g criterion ("a burst raises the rate of most units"); 0.4 and 0.6 are shown.

outcomes.statement: At the onset of seizure-like activity in S1 the LFP shows a large upwelling of delta power and an increase in theta amplitude, with theta activity aligned with bursts, and this holds at different electrodes.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 1; Figure 1i; Extended Data Fig. 3
outcomes.quote: These include a defined increase in the amplitude of theta-band oscillations, coherence between theta-band activity and bursting behavior, and a large upwelling in the delta-band frequency at epileptiform-like onset ... These characteristics remained present across different electrode sites
outcomes.notes: The criterion's onset, the first burst of the first epoch, falls at 0.73 to 0.90 s under the four burst readings, so only 0.73 to 0.90 s of baseline exists and the 2 s after onset lie within the 2 s e-folding half-width of the 0.5 Hz wavelet from the recording's start; these runs cannot test the claim, and the criterion fails there at all six electrodes (delta ratios 0.60 to 1.54, 0.1 to 100 Hz amplitude ratios 0.77 to 1.31, theta amplitude ratios 0.89 to 1.91). With onset at the paper's initiation burst (14.4 s, 5 s baseline), delta power in the 2 s after onset is 2.4 to 5.6 times the baseline at all six electrodes and the 0.1 to 100 Hz amplitude 2.09 to 2.97 times, so the criterion holds at three of three electrodes under both electrode readings with the broadband amplitude. With onset at the first epoch that has 5 s of recording before it, the criterion holds at three of three electrodes under burst reading b (onset 14.98 and 15.05 s) and at none or one under reading a (13.15 and 13.76 s, isolated bursts before the initiation). The theta amplitude never reaches twice the baseline (at most 1.92 times), so the statement's increase in theta amplitude holds only weakly. Whether the criterion's onset is the paper's is asked of a reader. The alignment of theta with bursts is tested in table2-phase-locking-counts.
deviations: Assumed onset at 14.4 s, the first burst of S1 as the paper's code sets it (sub-bursts at 14.4 to 14.91 s) and its figures show it (Extended Data Fig. 4c, baseline at 14.62 s; Fig. 4d, initiation from 14.67 s). The criterion's onset, the first burst of the first superburst under the fig1g readings, falls at 0.9 s, an event of two bursts at the recording's start, before the 5 s baseline the criterion asks for.
LFP is the 20-sample mean of the raw voltage (1 kHz), then 0.1 Hz high-pass (order 2) and 100 Hz low-pass (order 5), zero phase; wavelet cmor1-1 from PyWavelets, as the Methods name pycwt's.

outcomes.statement: In S1 theta-band activity shows no pattern at baseline, a standing wave oscillating across the length of the granule cell layer at initiation, and at the seizure stage a rolling wave orthogonal to the initiation direction, moving from the hilar to the outer aspect; S2 shows the same stages.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 1j; Extended Data Fig. 4c to 4e and Fig. 5c to 5d
outcomes.quote: During the initiation stage, theta propagations form a standing wave that oscillates across the length of the granule cell layer ... Following initiation and during all subsequent bursts, the theta oscillations form a rolling wave orthogonal to the direction observed during the initiation stage, moving along the granule cell layer from the hilar to outer aspect
outcomes.notes: Plane fits to arrival time explain little (R2 0.02 at initiation and 0.05 in the seizure stage of S1; 0.02 and 0.31 in S2). The initiation direction is 75 to 79 degrees from the layer's long axis in both slices, initiation and seizure directions differ by 4 to 16 degrees, and the seizure direction is 151 to 173 degrees from the outward normal (7 to 29 degrees from the inward normal, were the hilus on the convex side). In S1 the baseline R2 (0.000 to 0.001) is the lowest of the three stages; in S2 it (0.06 to 0.07) is above that of the code's initiation window. With a 250 ms S2 initiation window (one theta cycle) the initiation direction is 27 degrees from the long axis (R2 0.43) but 34 degrees from the seizure direction, outside 60 to 120. Filter order 4 and 5 give the same. Sign conventions of lag_matrix and plane_direction were checked by the verifier on a synthetic travelling wave.
deviations: Stage windows from the paper's figures and code (S1 initiation 14.4 to 14.91 s, seizure 15.0 to 28.0 s; S2 initiation 35.208 to 35.302 s, seizure 35.3 to 38.5 s; Extended Data Figs. 4 and 5, figures/figure_2/burst_peak_comparison.ipynb, figures/supplement/seizure_2/seizure2_burst_peaks.ipynb, printed with cell and line in the notebook). Bursting starts within the first second, so no window lies before the first burst; the baselines are stretches free of detected bursts under every reading just before initiation, S1 12.0 to 13.0 s and S2 34.45 to 35.2 s.
That the hilus lies on the concave side of the fitted layer is an assumption used for the outward direction; the other side is shown.

outcomes.statement: During seizure-like activity theta waves in S1 reach three electrodes along the propagation direction in turn, with a 40 ms delay from the first to the second and from the second to the third.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Fig. 4a and 4b legend
outcomes.quote: There is a 40ms delay between theta waves as they propagate from e1 to e2, and from e2 to e3.
outcomes.notes: Along the fitted seizure direction at 200 to 300 um the median lag is -23 ms (IQR -38 to -9, 13% positive); at 150 to 250 and 250 to 350 um, -19 and -23 ms. 19 to 34% of lags sit at the +-40 ms edge of the window. The sign is opposite to the fitted direction, which fig1j finds weakly defined. The reading with the figure's three electrodes could not be run.
deviations: The electrode spacing (about 200 to 300 um) is read from Extended Data Fig. 4a against its 500 um scale bar, an approximate reading.
The second reading of the criterion (the three electrodes of the figure) was not run; the map is drawn over histology without electrode coordinates.

outcomes.statement: In the two epileptiform slices, k-means clustering of electrodes by their pairwise theta lags gives spatial clusters that replicate the theta propagation of each stage, while the slices without epileptiform activity (S3 to S6) show no spatial pattern.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 4; Extended Data Fig. 4f to 4g, Fig. 5e and Fig. 6
outcomes.quote: For each stage of the recording, electrodes were clustered based on their average time delay between theta propagations ... Spatial maps of the electrode clusterings replicated the behavior seen in theta wave propagations ... The slices with no epileptiform-like activity (S3-S6) did not contain spatially coherent theta-band wave propagation patterns
outcomes.notes: Clusters are coherent beyond all 1000 shuffles in the S1 initiation (0.69 against a shuffle maximum of 0.57) and seizure stages (0.90 against 0.52) and in the S2 seizure stage (0.86 against 0.48), under both filter orders and all five seeds. The S2 initiation window of the code (94 ms, shorter than one theta cycle; median lag 0 ms, 0.2% of lags at the window edge) gives 0.84 against 0.86 and fails; every window of one theta cycle or longer passes under both filter orders and all five seeds (250 ms from 35.208 s, 0.92 to 0.93 against shuffle maxima of 0.64 to 0.65; 500 ms, 0.88 against 0.45 to 0.48; 1 s, 0.88 against 0.45 to 0.48; 35.0 to 35.5 s, 0.91 against 0.75 to 0.76), with 11 to 22% of lags at the edge. So the first part of the criterion holds once the S2 initiation window spans a theta cycle. S3 and S4 are less coherent (0.44 each, below their shuffle maxima 0.49 and 0.48), but S5 and S6 have no raw recording here, so the second part is shown for 2 of the 4 slices it names; partially reproduced under every initiation window. The S1 baseline is not coherent (0.37 against 0.44); the S2 baseline is (0.67 against 0.50), where the paper reports no pattern at baseline.
deviations: Stage windows as in fig1j-theta-propagation-stages; S2 initiation windows of 250 ms, 500 ms and 1 s from 35.208 s and 35.0 to 35.5 s as variants of the code's 94 ms window; for S3 and S4 the 8 s window with the most spikes (the paper's segments "with higher than average burst-like activity" have no stated length).
S5 and S6 not tested (raw recordings not in the dandiset).

outcomes.statement: The rolling wave appeared in every investigated burst of S1 and in about 75% of those of S2, 2 to 4 times per burst, giving about 200 stereotypic propagations in S1's seizure stage and 35 in S2's.
outcomes.source: Methods, Theta wave activity plots and videos, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: We saw this rolling wave in every burst we investigated from slice S1. The rolling wave was present in ~75% of the bursts we investigated from slice S2 ... The rolling wave pattern occurred 2–4 times per burst. Thus, over the six minute timespan of recordings from S1 and S2, there were approximately 200 stereotypic propagations in S1's seizure stage, and 35 in S2's.
outcomes.notes: The paper counted rolling waves by watching videos and gives no detector or list of bursts investigated. The criterion allows a detector built on the plane fits of fig1j-theta-propagation-stages; those fits explain 2 to 5% of the arrival-time variance in S1 and give initiation and seizure directions within 16 degrees of each other, so a detector built on them has no defensible basis. Run as the criterion defines it on S1's first seizure window (15 to 28 s), it finds no rolling wave. Of 63 theta cycles none has a plane fit with R2 above 0.5 (median 0.0023, largest 0.38), though 37 point within 45 degrees of the seizure direction, and none of the 7 to 22 bursts there has a rolling wave. Adopting it would give 0 for every expected value; it is not adopted. The question is put to the paper's authors (findings).

outcomes.statement: At the initiation stage of S1 the first burst splits into three sub-bursts whose peaks and troughs coincide with the theta oscillation, and the change in single-unit firing from sub-burst to sub-burst alternates between the same two spatial modes as theta; S2 shows a similar pattern.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 5; Figure 2a; Extended Data Fig. 5f
outcomes.quote: We found that theta-band oscillations during the initiation stage of S1 are temporally aligned with sub-bursts in single unit spiking activity ... Calculating the change in single unit firing from sub-burst to sub-burst produced heatmaps with similar spatiotemporal oscillations to those seen in theta-band propagations.
outcomes.notes: In S1 the cluster difference in firing change is 0.22 then 0.91 Hz (no flip) and the theta difference between clusters is 0.24, -0.26 and -0.65 uV over the three sub-bursts. In S2 the firing difference flips (3.90 then -7.06 Hz) but the theta difference does not alternate (4.68, 2.45, -0.76 uV). The S2 initiation clusters come from the code's 94 ms window, which fails the coherence test in ext4-electrode-lag-clusters; with the clusters of the 250 ms window the firing difference flips (-8.92 then 5.51 Hz) and theta again does not alternate (-7.20, -4.42, 1.14 uV). The sub-burst times are printed beside their source lines in the code (burst_peak_comparison.ipynb cell 5, seizure2_burst_peaks.ipynb cell 7); the S2 sub-bursts last 26 to 37 ms, a fraction of one theta cycle.

outcomes.statement: Significantly theta phase-locked units are 70 of 212 (33%) in the S1 KA recording and 101 of 180 (56%) in the S2 KA recording, against 14 of 249, 2 of 51, 8 of 87, 6 of 109, 8 of 136 and 1 of 100 in the other recordings.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Table 2; Results, paragraph 6
outcomes.inferred: Counts from Extended Data Table 2, an image in the supplement PDF; the text states only the averages (see table2-phase-locking-seizure-vs-not).
outcomes.notes: With the Methods' spike selection, S1 KA 60 (70 expected) and S2 KA 104 (101); recordings 2, 4, 5 and 6 give 19, 5, 11 and 3 over the whole recording and 12, 0, 10 and 5 over the code's spans (14, 2, 8, 6 expected); 1 or 2 of 6 counts within tolerance, and S1 misses, so the partial clause fails too. With the code's cycle selection (variant) S1 73 and S2 107 match, 3 to 4 of 6 are within tolerance, and over the code's spans the other recordings are below 10% (5.5 to 8.0%). With the RMS taken over the whole recording (the criterion's "RMS of the whole series"), S1 gives 59 and S2 104, and the other recordings 19, 5, 11 and 3 (whole recording) or 12, 0, 8 and 5 (code's spans), 1 or 3 of 6 within tolerance, and S1 misses under every envelope reading. Recordings 7 and 8 cannot be tested (no raw recording). Spikes shifted within the seizure windows give 10 of 212 and 15 of 180 significant, near chance.
deviations: LFP is the 20-sample mean of the raw voltage (1 kHz) where the paper used its own filtered, downsampled pickles.

The code's spans are the start and stop times in the names of the LFP files it saved (data/ephys_raw at commit 0f83f70, printed in the notebook; the get_raw_data notebooks list only some of them). They are in file time (the S4 span 145 to 155 s lies beyond the 130 s sorting) and are moved to the sorting's clock by the offsets of the link.
Theta is filtered within each window, as the code filters each saved window (TJ_phase_locking_basics.ipynb cell 3 line 107, printed in the notebook).

The RMS that the envelope must exceed is taken over the analysed windows (for recordings 1 and 3, the seizure windows), as the code computes it on its saved windows; the criterion and the Methods say "the RMS of the whole time series", which is run as a second reading with the RMS of theta over the whole recording. Both give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: During seizure-like activity on average 45% of units per recording are phase locked, against 5% in recordings without seizure-like activity; within S1 and S2, only 5% and 4% are phase locked outside the seizure periods.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Table 2 legend; Extended Data Fig. 8c to 8d; Results, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: During seizure-like activity, on average, 45% of neurons per recording are phase locked. This is considerably higher than the 5% average seen in recordings with no seizure-like activity. In the recordings that expressed seizure-like behavior, average phase locking was considerably higher in the portions of the recording with epileptiform activity, compared to the portions without
outcomes.notes: Seizure mean 43.0% with the Methods' selection (46.9% with the code's), within tolerance. Outside the seizure windows 5.2% (S1, within) and 4.4% (S2, 8 of 180, just above the 4.4% bound). The mean over recordings 2, 4, 5 and 6 is 8.2% over whole recordings and 5.2% over the code's spans; at most three of the four values match under one reading, and every value other than the seizure mean is below 10%, the partial clause. Recordings 7 and 8 are not in the mean. With the RMS over the whole recording the values are 42.8%, 8.2% or 4.7%, 5.7% and 3.9%, 2 or 3 of 4 within tolerance, and every value other than the seizure mean is below 10%. Measured is the Methods' selection with whole recordings.
deviations: The mean over recordings without seizure-like activity uses 4 of the paper's 6 recordings.
The RMS for the spike selection as in table2-phase-locking-counts (analysed windows, and the whole recording as a second reading).

outcomes.statement: In S1 the significantly phase-locked units form two spatial groups along the granule cell layer whose preferred theta phases differ significantly (Kuiper test).
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 6; Figure 2b; Extended Data Fig. 8a
outcomes.quote: Clustering based on the two modes of significant units yielded two groups with significantly different phase angles

statistics.about: phase angles of the two clusters of phase-locked units, S1
statistics.n: 70 significant units of S1 (33 and 28 after removing duplicate positions, per the code)

outcomes.notes: With the 60 units significant in the seizure windows, the Methods' split by angular difference from the polar mode (reading b) gives Kuiper p below 1e-4; this split separates the angles by construction, so its test is bound to be significant. The spatial splits give p = 0.037 (code thresholds, 32 and 26 units after removing duplicate positions) and 0.11 (k-means on position). With the code's spike selection the spatial splits give 0.0042 and 0.0014, and with units significant over the whole recording 0.035 to 0.051 (Methods) and 0.0008 to 0.013 (code). With the 59 units significant under the RMS of the whole recording the spatial splits give 0.023 and 0.020. The statement's two spatial groups with different phases are supported at p <= 0.01 only with the code's spike selection; under the Methods' selection the outcome rests on reading b alone. Whether reading b, which cannot fail, is a reading of the paper is asked of a reader.
deviations: The polar mode is taken from a 36-bin histogram, a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: Hierarchical clustering of the STTC matrix of S1 gives two groups of units that divide the granule cell layer into the same two spatial modes, and S2 gives a similar result.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 7; Figure 2c; Extended Data Fig. 5h
outcomes.quote: Two groupings of neuronal populations were created by performing hierarchical clustering on the spike time tiling coefficient (STTC) matrix ... A spatial map of the neuronal clusters divides the granule cell layer into the same two modes seen in previous plots. Similar results were observed in the second epileptiform-like slice (S2)
outcomes.notes: S2 holds (133 and 47 units, positions differ, Mann-Whitney p = 0.002; the half-distance variant p = 0.0001). S1 does not (151 and 61 units, p = 0.26; variants 0.20 to 0.59), though the S1 split lies on the same side as the code's phase-cluster thresholds. The criterion holds for one of the two slices.

outcomes.statement: The first eigenvector of the STTC matrix, mapped onto the units, forms a gradient across the granule cell layer in both S1 and S2, reproducing the hierarchical clusters.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 7; Extended Data Fig. 9f to 9h; Methods, Eigendecomposition for neural spatial clustering
outcomes.quote: A second clustering method based on the eigendecomposition of the STTC matrix reproduced these results
outcomes.notes: S2 holds (Spearman rho = 0.51, p = 3.6e-13; clusters differ, p = 7.8e-11). In S1 the first eigenvector differs between clusters (p = 4.2e-29) but not with position (rho = 0.08, p = 0.26); the second eigenvector correlates with position (rho = -0.35, p = 2.4e-7), a variant outside the criterion.

outcomes.statement: For S1, the STTC matrix has larger eigenvalues and a lower reconstruction error than the correlation matrix of the spike trains.
outcomes.source: Methods, Eigendecomposition for neural spatial clustering; Extended Data Fig. 9c and 9d
outcomes.quote: For our data, the STTC matrix had higher eigenvalues and a lower reconstruction error when compared to correlation.
outcomes.notes: All 20 eigenvalues are larger for STTC (16.6 against 8.3 for the first) and the relative reconstruction error is lower for every k from 1 to 20 (0.70 against 0.87 at k = 1, 0.53 against 0.76 at k = 20). The STTC matrix has negative eigenvalues (smallest -2.64).

outcomes.statement: Of about 45,000 neuron pairs in S1, 784 have a significant directed latency and form the circuit diagram; the other recordings give 1940 (S2 KA), 304 (S1 baseline), 37 (S2 baseline), 79 (S3), 37 (S4), 172 (S5) and 92 (S6) significant pairs.
outcomes.source: Methods, Definition of circuit diagram propagation vector; Figure 3a; Extended Data Fig. 10 and 11a
outcomes.quote: Of the 45,000 neuronal pairs of neurons in slice S1, 784 pairs were classified as significant.
outcomes.notes: All eight counts equal the paper's. S1 has 44,944 candidate pairs (212 squared). Changing the STTC threshold or the minimum number of latencies moves the S1 count to 667 to 841.
deviations: A pair whose forward latencies fail the count or mean rule is not reversed, as in the code's curate_latencies (hc112823_acid.ipynb).

outcomes.statement: The latency-weighted propagation angle histograms are bipolar (two modes 180 degrees apart, aligned with the initiation theta propagation) for the epileptiform slices S1 and S2, unimodal for the other dentate gyrus slices S3 and S4, and bimodal but not bipolar (two orthogonal directions) for the CA1 slices S5 and S6.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraphs 9 and 10; Figure 3a and 3c; Extended Data Fig. 10
outcomes.quote: For slice S1, the angle histogram was bipolar, which we define as angular pairwise correlations that are 180° out of phase ... None of the non-epileptiform-like slices displayed the bimodal circuit diagram observed from the epileptiform-like slices. Both of the non-epileptiform-like dentate gyrus slices (S3 and S4) had a unimodal circuit diagram ... The slices from CA1 (S5 and S6) had evenly distributed circuit diagrams and a bimodal, but not bipolar, angle histogram
outcomes.notes: S1 and S2 are bipolar (modes 180 degrees apart; R2 0.52 and 0.68 against R1 0.12 and 0.10), and no other slice is. S3 and S4 are not unimodal by the measure (two peaks 67.5 degrees apart, second 0.92 and 0.70 of the first; R1 0.34 and 0.35 above R2 0.15 and 0.26). S5 and S6 have peaks 45 and 135 degrees apart. 2 of 6 slices are in their stated class. Unit positions lie on a 17.5 um grid, so 8 to 24% of the latency weight falls exactly on the 22.5 degree bin edges, and flipping y does not mirror the histogram. With y flipped or the bins shifted by half a bin, S1 and S2 stay bipolar and no other slice becomes bipolar, while S4, S5 and S6 change class (3 or 4 of 6 in their stated class); S3 and S4 are never unimodal. The partial outcome holds under all four.
deviations: One dominant peak is read as the second-largest local maximum being below half the largest; the claims file does not define it.

outcomes.statement: In S1 and S2 the baseline recordings before kainic acid show the same bipolar circuit as the recordings during epileptiform activity, suggesting a structural property of the slices.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 10; Extended Data Fig. 10a to 10d
outcomes.quote: For both S1 and S2, the non-epileptiform-like recordings prior to administering kainic acid had the same circuit diagram as during epileptiform-like activity
outcomes.notes: Both baseline recordings are bipolar (S1 R2 0.34 against R1 0.08; S2 0.67 against 0.32), with modes 0 and 0 degrees (S1) and 0 and 22 degrees (S2) from the KA recording's modes.

outcomes.statement: The circuit geometry test gives p-values orders of magnitude smaller for the slices with recurrent circuits (S1 KA 9.7e-20, S1 baseline 8.6e-13, S2 KA 1.6e-68, S2 baseline 1.0e-6) than for the others (S3 0.12, S4 0.37, S5 0.00042, S6 0.0011), so the bipolar circuits are not an artefact of where the neurons lie.
outcomes.source: Results, last paragraph; Figure 3b; Extended Data Table 3; Methods, Statistical test of circuit geometry
outcomes.quote: If the bipolar plots from epileptiform-like slices were produced by bias in neuronal geometry, the test's p -values would be similar for all slices, however, we found the epileptiform-like slices to be orders of magnitude more significant

statistics.about: positions of positive against negative angle connections, S1 KA (Figure 3b)

outcomes.notes: With y as stored all eight -log10 p are within tolerance; with y flipped 2 of 8. Under both, the largest p of S1 and S2 is 400 to 4600 times smaller than the smallest p of S3 to S6.

outcomes.statement: In a simplified dentate gyrus network model, increasing recurrent connectivity between granule cells produces seizure-like bursting.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 8; Discussion, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 12; Methods, Simulation of epileptiform behavior
outcomes.quote: We constructed an in silico model to simulate functional connectivity within the dentate gyrus ( Extended Data Fig. 12 ) 48 and found that increasing pairwise interactions between granule cells produced seizure-like bursting events.
outcomes.notes: The simulation needs NEST with a neuron model compiled by NESTML; the code pins conda nest-simulator 3.4 and nestml 5 (environment.yml), which the registry's pip lock cannot provide. Tried with PyPI nest-simulator 3.10.0. NESTML 9.0.1 fails to parse the model (models/izh_cond_exp2syn.nestml uses the older keyword "neuron"), and NESTML 5 fails against NEST 3.10 (nest.ll_api has no sli_func). The sweep itself (275 simulations of 30 s) was not timed.

findings.statement: The raw recordings of slices S5 and S6 (the paper's recordings 7 and 8, 136 and 100 units) are not in the dandiset. Their sortings fall on the electrode layouts of the sub-3C and sub-8D files, but none of those files aligns with their spike times, so the phase locking and electrode clustering of the CA1 slices cannot be repeated from the dandiset.

The dandiset holds raw voltage only. The curated spike sortings that every analysis of the paper uses are not in it; they are in the paper's GitHub repository, in three formats (acqm zips, Phy zips and pickled braingeneers SpikeData objects that need that package or a custom reader).

No file records the experimental condition (baseline, zero magnesium, kainic acid, optogenetic stimulation) or when kainic acid was applied; session descriptions are empty and there are no epochs, intervals or stimulus series. Which file is the S1 or S2 baseline or KA recording can only be found from the sortings, and the latency from KA to seizure-like activity cannot be measured.
The session start times of all 69 files are the conversion date (2024-09-28), not the recording dates (2022 and 2023 in the paper's repository).

Subjects are named by slice with patient letters that differ from the paper's (the paper's patient A, 52 F, is sub-10F; patient C, 20 M, is sub-1A), electrode locations are all "unknown", and the hippocampal region of each slice (dentate gyrus or CA1) is not given.

Two analysed recordings are parts of longer files. The S1 baseline sorting starts 20.0 s into sub-10F-0 and the S4 sorting 30.0 s into sub-9E-2; nothing in the dandiset or the paper states the offsets, which were found by aligning spikes with the raw voltage.

Recordings 1 to 6 of the paper are in the dandiset and align exactly with the paper's sortings (offset scan peaks 74 to 169 times chance), and with those sortings the circuit-pair counts of all eight recordings equal the paper's and the geometry-test p-values match Extended Data Table 3.

Five files of one slice, sub-3C-1 to sub-3C-5, are saturated at the limits of the converter (0 or 1023 counts, up to 88% of samples) at the same seconds of each file, 10 to 12 (13 in sub-3C-5) and 20 to 21 s, and sub-3C-0 at 3 to 5 and 8 to 9 s; nothing in the files records a stimulus or other cause. The files are not copies of one recording. Over the first 40 s and all 972 channels their identical samples lie in the saturated seconds (26 to 27% of samples there, 4% elsewhere) and their LFP correlates at a median of 0.03 to 0.08 outside them, though sub-3C-1 to sub-3C-4 share 78 to 82% of samples in one second of saturation (10 to 11 s, 64 channels). No analysis here uses these files.

It did not open the paper's repository or the NWB files.

disagreements.reason: At the criterion's onset (0.895 s) the baseline is under 1 s and nothing holds; that stretch sits in the edge region of the 0.5 Hz wavelet, so that run is not a valid failure. At the paper's initiation time (14.4 s, the author's addition) delta rises at 6 of 6 electrodes and broadband amplitude is above 2x at 6 of 6 (2.1 to 3.0), but theta amplitude never reaches 2x (at most 1.66). The only valid run uses 14.4 s, which the criterion does not name (problem 2). It asked for the criterion's onset under the other three burst readings, with the baseline that exists before it.

Under the code's cycle selection, recordings 1 and 3 match (73, 107), and recordings 2, 4, 5 and 6 stay below 10% with the code's spans (8.0, 5.9, 5.7, 5.5%). Recording 2 never reaches 14 +- 1.4, and recordings 7 and 8 are untested. Moving the code's spans from file time to sorting time is an inference, plausible; theta is filtered per window, which adds edge effects in 10 s windows (problem 11). It could not check the seizure windows, the code's spans or the thresholds in the repository.

verifications.reviewed: The full executed notebooks after round 1 (reproduce_elliott_2026.ipynb and lfp_elliott_2026.ipynb) with their conclusions and summaries, the helper module, the claims file, this attempt record and the paper's full text. It also noted that finding 5's "electrode locations are all 'unknown'" was not shown by any printed output; the data check of the spike notebook now prints the locations of the electrodes tables of all 69 files (only "unknown").

paper_notes.statement: The Methods state that the STTC matrix is positive semidefinite and interpret its eigendecomposition like PCA; the S1 STTC matrix has negative eigenvalues (smallest -2.64).

Question for the authors. How were bursts and superbursts detected for the counts of 67 bursts and 11 superbursts (S1) and 47 bursts (S2), and for the 6 to 8 bursts per epoch? Neither the paper nor its code defines them; the readings named in the claims file (population-rate peaks above twice a pre-KA mean or the mean plus 3 SD, gaps under 5 s) give 124 to 353 bursts and 12 epochs in S1.

Question for the authors. Which spike selection produced Extended Data Table 2? The Methods keep spikes while the theta envelope exceeds the RMS; the code keeps spikes in theta cycles whose peak exceeds the RMS of the envelope. Here the code's selection gives 73 and 107 phase-locked units in the S1 and S2 seizure windows (70 and 101 reported) and the Methods' gives 60 and 104.

Question for the authors. How were the two phase clusters of Fig. 2b formed for the Kuiper test? The Methods partition units by their angular difference from the polar mode, which makes the angle distributions differ by construction; the code sets position thresholds by hand. Was p = 0.01 from a spatial split?

Question for the authors. How were the onset of seizure-like activity, the stage windows, the propagation directions and the rolling waves defined and counted? The paper shows them in videos and the code sets times by hand; here the onset was assumed at the first burst the code splits into sub-bursts (14.4 s in S1), and plane fits to theta lags did not recover distinct initiation and seizure directions.

The simulation of Extended Data Fig. 12 pins conda nest-simulator 3.4 and nestml 5. With the NEST available from PyPI (3.10) neither NESTML 9 (cannot parse the model's syntax) nor NESTML 5 (calls an API NEST 3.10 removed) compiles the model, so the code does not run outside that conda environment.

entries.title: Optogenetic inhibition in human hippocampal slices on HD-MEAs (Andrews, Geng, Voitiuk et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Andrews, Geng, Voitiuk et al. (2024) on dandiset 001132, which holds 69 raw HD-MEA voltage recordings of 12 human hippocampal slices from 7 patients. The files hold no sorted units, light events or condition labels, so only the cohort claim is tested; the notebook surveys every recording, recovers light periods of slices 3C, 4C and 7D from the voltage, shows a threshold-crossing variant for those of 3C, and runs the paper's network model.
